intro: A pattern longer than k is searched in scope `long` (SPEC-pattern-search section 7.7): each orientation anchors on its own window of k bases (P's first k for `forward`, the reverse complement's first k for `reverse`), the anchors are counted (`counts.anchors`) and, without an opt-in, nothing more is done: `counts.paths` is `unknown`, the list withheld with `paths_later_increment` and the entry carries that note (the answer of `long_search: anchors`, the field's default). With `long_search: paths` (section 12.1) the extension is admitted when the anchors are `exact` and at most `max_anchors` (the host's default 1,000) and extends every anchor base by base along the graph's edges, depth first, keeping the bases the pattern allows: every complete walk of L - k + 1 k-mers is a *path*, released when the paths are `exact` and at most `max_paths` (1,024 on this host) in `all_or_count`, the first `max_paths` in `partial`; a path need not lie in one record. `counts.paths.extension` says what the extension did (`completed`, `no_anchors`, `stopped`, `not_started`, `not_admitted`). The stops gain the phase `extension` and the reason `max_memory`: the walks the extension keeps for the release, and without labels each path's result object, are charged to the request's memory account (`max_memory_mb`, section 12.1), and a walk that does not fit stops the extension, `partial` releasing the walks kept before it (`cut` `max_memory`).

Three notions of support are kept apart, from weakest to strongest, because a walk of the graph need not come from any one genome. A *path* is a walk of the graph spelling the pattern: its k-mers exist in the index, but each may come from a different record (a *mosaic*: two records sharing a repeat make a walk through it that neither holds whole, section 20.1). *Label support* at the `label_intersection` level says that one label (a taxid column, a header) annotates every k-mer of the walk: the label's records together carry all its pieces, and nothing says that one record holds the walk contiguously. *Record-verified support* (`record_verified`) says that one record of the label holds the whole walk at consecutive coordinates, placed as an occurrence over the L bases: the one claim about a contiguous recorded sequence (I.1). A hypothetical case: a 60-base pattern whose first 45 bases occur in one record and whose last 45 bases in another record of the same taxid column (two strains of one species, say), the two overlapping on 30 shared bases, is spelled by a path, since every one of its k-mers lies in one record or the other; the taxid column annotates every k-mer, so the path has label support at the `label_intersection` level; yet no single record holds the 60 bases, so neither record verifies it and no `record_verified` label is listed. The table compares what each notion counts, what connects the k-mers and what the request options change.

In this chapter the distinction is described, not discriminated: every window is its record's own path, so no synthetic mosaic is searched, no `label_intersection` label is observed beside a `record_verified` one, and no rejection of a mosaic is claimed (the coverage gap above lists it among what is not exercised). With `output.labels: all` each released path lists the labels on every one of its k-mers, each with its support as the table has it (section 12.1); `require_support: record_verified` lists the verified labels only. A *supported path* (`long_search: supported_paths`, section 20) is a walk some label supports along its whole length, found by a search that carries the support of each branch and prunes a branch whose support runs out, at the `record_verified` level on this index (`supported_paths_level` `best`) or at `label_intersection` on request; its count is `counts.supported_paths`, its rows are read in every mode under `max_annotation_work`, the memory account and the deadline, and a predicate (section 20.9) selects among the supported walks on the support they carry (`predicate_strands` `context`: the walk as spelled, no mirror read). An exact pattern that sdust flags over its whole text carries the note `low_complexity_pattern`, stated beside a completed search or a threshold stop and never beside a budget stop of the search (section 7.8).

Ground truth: windows of 32 to 2,000 bases cut from the records of I.2 as chapter P cuts them (A, C, G, T only, unique on both strands of the fetched span, a DUST score below 2.0 over their first 64 bases; the long windows below 3.0), so that the record's own path is known: the window's bases on strand `+` as one walk of L - k + 1 k-mers, `instance` equal to `sequence` and `offset` 0 (`path_spells`), verified by the record's taxid at the window's 1-based coordinates (`path_record_verified`). Whether other walks of the graph spell the window (a mosaic through a repeat two records share) is not modelled: the path count is bounded below by one. The homopolymers A^60, T^100 and A^100000 are not record windows: a homopolymer is a self-loop of the graph, one k-mer with an edge to itself, so its path is that node repeated. Every request names `mode`, `max_contexts` 10,000 and `time_budget_ms` 60,000 and the host's defaults as in chapter P; the supported-path requests name `max_paths` 1,024, the service's ceiling and the host's cap. Via MCP (`pattern_search`) a pattern longer than k without `long_search` is refused at submit (the anchors-only answer is not expressible), a pattern above 1,000 characters is refused whatever `long_search` says, `max_annotation_work` and `max_memory_mb` have no argument, a cap of 0 is refused, and the strand words are mapped by the runner; `max_paths` is always sent (the host's cap when the request names none). Each by-design cell names its case; appendix B gives the service's code and text.

L-paths.title: paths
L-paths.prose: Windows of 32, 40, 60, 100 and 200 bases of 15 records, three per length (32 bp: sau, hvo, pfa; 40 bp: cel, mtb, mpn; 60 bp: cal, drem, hiv1; 100 bp: cje, sso, ath; 200 bp: lam, sco, ser), with `long_search: paths` in `all_or_count`: a path spells the window on strand `+` with `instance` equal to its `sequence`, `offset` 0 and L - k + 1 nodes (`path_spells`); the path count is `exact` and at least 1 (`count_relation`: `exact` is the relation the answer declares about its own extension, 1 the record's own path computed from the record; no index-wide total is verified); `extension` `completed` and `scope` `long` (`entry_fields`). 32 bp is the shortest pattern longer than k, one base of extension beyond the anchor. The rows group the tests by length and the record changes with it: correctness controls across lengths and records, not a runtime-versus-length benchmark. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted} test{n_footnoted:s} did not pass on every access path: {footnoted_text}; the detail block{n_footnoted:s} follow{n_footnoted:v} the table. | In this run every test passed on every access path.]]
L-paths.claim: a window longer than k is spelled by a path of the graph, the extension completed

L-verified.title: record-verified
L-verified.prose: Windows of 40, 60 and 100 bp of six records with few relatives in RefSeq (buc, mge, mpn, ser, mja, sso), with `long_search: paths`, `output.labels: all` and `require_support: record_verified`: the path spelling the window lists the record's taxid with support `record_verified` and an occurrence of the record at the window's 1-based coordinates on `+`, every occurrence of that label inside its record (`path_record_verified`). This is the verification of section 12.1, the chains of consecutive coordinates placed record by record, read from the answer; the check never reads a label the answer does not list. This is record-verified support, the one claim of a contiguous recorded sequence (Background); every window being its record's own path, a label-supported mosaic that no record verifies is not exercised here.
L-verified.claim: a record verifies its own path at the window's coordinates

L-supported.title: supported paths
L-supported.prose: Eight windows of 40, 60, 100 and 200 bp (mtb, buc, hvo, scem; hsam, lam, bsu, cje) searched as supported paths with a predicate `any` of the record's taxid (`predicate_only`, `predicate_strands` `context`, `max_paths` 1,024): the record's path is among the selected supported paths, verified by the taxid at the window's coordinates, and `counts.supported_paths` is at least 1; and two 60 bp windows at the `label_intersection` level (`supported_paths_level`): the record's path spelled and the level echoed in the counts. The two levels are the Background's: at `best`, `record_verified` on this index, a supported path is one some record holds whole; at `label_intersection` it is one whose k-mers a label's records carry between them, the weaker claim (the walk need not lie in one record, and the check reads the level, not a record). The search reads the annotation in every mode, so these are also the chapter's tests of the row reads under the account and the work budget. The rows group the tests by level and length.
L-supported.claim: the record's walk is a supported path at both levels, selected by the record's taxid

L-anchors.title: anchors
L-anchors.prose: Three 45 bp windows without `long_search` (the default `anchors`): `counts.anchors` exact and at least 1, `counts.paths` `unknown`, the list withheld `paths_later_increment` and the note stated (section 7.7). Via MCP the service refuses a pattern longer than k without `long_search` at submit, so the anchors-only answer is by design not shown there (appendix B).
L-anchors.claim: without an opt-in a long pattern is answered by its anchors only, the paths unknown and withheld

L-caps.title: caps
L-caps.prose: On a 50 bp window of H. volcanii: `partial` with `max_paths` 0 (nothing returned, `cut` `max_paths`); `all_or_count` with `max_paths` 0 (`withheld` `count_above_threshold`); `supported_paths` with `max_annotation_work` 10 (the search's reads stop: `stop` in the phase `extension` with the reason `max_annotation_work`, `withheld` `annotation_budget`), and the same in `partial` (`cut` `max_annotation_work`). Via MCP a cap of 0 is refused at submit and `max_annotation_work` has no argument (appendix B).
L-caps.claim: max_paths and max_annotation_work stop, cut or withhold exactly as stated

L-memory.title: memory
L-memory.prose: A^100000 with `long_search: paths` in `partial` under `max_memory_mb` 1. The input is a long walk through one repeated node: a homopolymer is a self-loop of the graph, so its single path has L - k + 1 nodes, each the same k-mer. Storing that path for the release, the walk the extension keeps or the result object built from it, is charged to the request's memory account and exceeds one megabyte, so the answer must state the documented stop: the phase `extension` or `output` with the reason `max_memory`, the list cut `max_memory`, and the note `low_complexity_pattern` absent beside a budget stop of the search (sections 7.8 and 12.1). What this bounds is the request's own account, the bytes the host charges to this request for the paths it keeps: not the graph, the process or the container's resident memory, which the load lines of this document report in gigabytes (I.4, Timing 6) and which this test neither measures nor certifies. The stop may come in either phase: the expectation accepts both, and the phase this run recorded is in the row's detail (direct-local: “{x[L-memory-0001][dl][checks][stop][evidence]}”), not a proof that both were exercised. Timing class slow. Not exercised via MCP: the tool has no `max_memory_mb` argument (see B), so no MCP call reaches the host before the direct access paths[[n_cold_dl ? ({n_cold_dl} host-cold direct-local execution{n_cold_dl:s} in this run)]].
L-memory.claim: the memory account stops a path search and says so

L-long.title: long windows
L-long.prose: Two units. L-long-length: windows of 500 bp (buc, hvo), 1,000 bp (mja) and 2,000 bp (cal) with paths, drawn with the DUST threshold raised to 3.0, the marker-gene lengths of the verification: the record's path is listed and the path count is exact and at least 1. L-long-other, where the v4 and the v5 evidence differ: 100 bp of M. pneumoniae as its reverse complement with `strands` `reverse`, and a 60 bp IUPAC pattern of S. solfataricus with three two-base codes at positions 10, 30 and 50 with paths. [[manifest_version = 5 ? In this manifest both also check the spelled path: the record's path listed as `-` for the reverse window and the record's own `+` path among the IUPAC pattern's (`path_spells`). | In manifest v4 both require a path count of at least 1 and nothing more: a green cell there establishes a nonzero path count, not that the returned path spells the record's bases on the intended strand, which no v4 check of these two rows reads (the `path_spells` witness of L-long-length is not applied to them). Manifest v5 adds `path_spells` on the record's strand to both; that is a later version's check, not part of this run's evidence.]] And A^60 with paths and `max_anchors` 1: an exact anchor window is one k-mer per orientation, so its anchors are A^31 on `+` and T^31 on `-`, exactly 2, above the threshold, and the extension is not admitted (`withheld` `anchors_above_threshold`, `extension` `not_admitted`; code-derived). Via MCP the 2,000 bp window is refused at submit, above the service's 1,000 characters (appendix B).
L-long.claim: long windows[[manifest_version = 5 ?, the reverse strand, IUPAC codes]] and the anchor threshold behave as section 12.1 states[[manifest_version = 5 ? |, and the reverse-strand and IUPAC windows answer at least one path (their spelled path unverified in v4)]]

L-repeat.title: homopolymers
L-repeat.prose: A^60 and T^100 with paths: the note `low_complexity_pattern` stated (sdust flags the whole text; the search completed, no budget stop) and the path count exact and at least 1, the self-loop's path.
L-repeat.claim: a homopolymer carries the low-complexity note and its self-loop path

L-paths.property: A 32 to 200 bp window of the record with long_search paths: a path spells it on + (instance equal to sequence, offset 0, L - k + 1 nodes), the path count exact and at least 1, the extension completed.
L-paths.note: The rows group the tests by length; the record changes with the length: correctness controls across lengths and records, not a runtime-versus-length benchmark (latency varies across records; these controls do not isolate the effect of window length).
L-paths.question: Does a window longer than k come back as a path spelling it, the extension completed?

L-verified.property: paths with labels all and require_support record_verified: the record's taxid carries the path spelling the window with support record_verified and an occurrence at the window's 1-based coordinates on +.
L-verified.question: Does the record verify its own path at the window's coordinates (a contiguous occurrence, not label support alone)?

L-supported.property: Supported paths selected by a predicate any of the record's taxid (predicate_only): the record's path among them, verified by the taxid (record_verified: a contiguous occurrence), counts.supported_paths at least 1; at the label_intersection level the record's path spelled and the level echoed (label support alone: no record is claimed to hold the walk).
L-supported.question: Is the record's walk a supported path at both levels, selected by its taxid?

L-anchors.property: A 45 bp pattern without long_search: the anchors counted exact (at least 1), the paths unknown, the list withheld paths_later_increment with the note.
L-anchors.question: Without the opt-in, is a long pattern answered by its anchors alone, the paths unknown and withheld?

L-caps.property: max_paths 0 cuts (partial, cut max_paths) or withholds (all_or_count, count_above_threshold); max_annotation_work 10 stops a supported-path search (stop extension / max_annotation_work: withheld annotation_budget, or cut max_annotation_work in partial).
L-caps.question: Do max_paths and max_annotation_work cut, withhold or stop exactly as stated?

L-memory.property: A^100000 on a self-loop with paths and max_memory_mb 1 in partial: the request's memory account (not the process or the container memory) stops the search in the phase extension or output with the reason max_memory, the list cut max_memory, no low-complexity note beside the budget stop.
L-memory.question: Does the request's memory account stop a path search and say so?

L-long-length.property: A 500 to 2,000 bp window with paths: the record's path listed, the path count exact and at least 1.
L-long-length.question: Is a 500 to 2,000 bp window spelled by the record's path?

L-long-other.property: [[manifest_version = 5 ? A reverse-complement window under strands reverse is the record's path as - (path_spells on -); a 60 bp IUPAC pattern's paths hold the record's + path | A reverse-complement window under strands reverse and a 60 bp IUPAC pattern with paths each answer a path count of at least 1; no v4 check reads the spelled path or its strand (v5 adds path_spells on the record's strand: not this run's evidence)]]; A^60 with max_anchors 1 counts its two anchors (A^31, T^31) exactly and admits no extension (anchors_above_threshold).
L-long-other.question: Do a reverse-strand window and an IUPAC pattern answer at least one path, and does max_anchors 1 refuse the extension of a two-anchor homopolymer?

L-repeat.property: A homopolymer of 60 or 100 with paths carries the note low_complexity_pattern and its path count is exact and at least 1.
L-repeat.question: Does a homopolymer carry the low-complexity note and its self-loop path?

units.L-memory: Not exercised via MCP: the `pattern_search` tool has no `max_memory_mb` argument; see B.

purpose: A pattern longer than k cannot sit in one k-mer, so /pattern answers a second question for it: which walks of the graph spell the whole pattern, and does any record hold such a walk contiguously? The answer is a count of anchors (the k-mers where the pattern can begin) and, on request, the *paths* that spell it, each with the labels that support it at one of two levels, or the *supported paths* alone. This chapter's evidence is a known witness: a window cut from a record must come back as its record's path, record-verified at the window's coordinates where the request asks for it; the caps, the memory account and the anchor threshold must act as the contract states; what the tools cannot express is said so.

intro_tables.caption: the three notions of path support, from weakest to strongest (SPEC-pattern-search sections 12.1 and 20.1); a user seeking a contiguous recorded sequence asks for the option record_verified
rows: `counts.paths`: the walks of L - k + 1 k-mers spelling the pattern
the graph's edges alone: consecutive k-mers overlap by k - 1 bases, whatever records they come from
no: a path may be a mosaic
the search: the anchors are extended into walks; without labels nothing is said about records
`counts.labels.by_support.label_intersection`: the labels on every k-mer of a released path
one label annotates each k-mer (the intersection of the rows)
no: the label's records together carry the pieces
`output.labels: all` lists the labels of released paths with their support (the search unchanged); `supported_paths_level: label_intersection` prunes a supported-path search on this level
`counts.labels.by_support.record_verified` and `counts.occurrences`: the labels one record verifies, and the placed occurrences
one record's consecutive coordinates over the whole walk (the record mapping)
yes: one record holds the L bases at one place

`require_support: record_verified` lists the verified labels only (the search unchanged); `long_search: supported_paths` prunes the search to the walks some label supports, at `best`, which is `record_verified` on this index
